attempt.narrative: Cleaner line than the prior win. T1 Fake Out flinched Slaking while Weezing Protected the Psychic. T2 that same Psychic killed Weezing from full, Intimidate finally resolved as the Gas dropped, and Parting Shot took Slaking to -2 Attack / -1 Sp. Atk and pivoted Incineroar out for Spiritomb. Indeedee arrived with Psychic Terrain; Shadow Ball whiffed on it (my error - Indeedee-F is Psychic/NORMAL, so Ghost is 0x) but Dark Pulse took it to 61. T4 Indeedee used Follow Me, pulled Focus Blast off Slaking and died to it, and Slaking's critical High Horsepower removed Alakazam. Gengar answered Porygon2's slot; Taunt denied Recover and Dark Pulse finished it on T7, though Thunderbolt left Gengar on 3 HP and paralyzed. Weavile replaced Gengar, Knock Off removed Meloetta and its Life Orb on T9 while Will-O-Wisp burned the loafing Slaking, Triple Axel removed Mega Staraptor on its transformation turn, and a Mega Scizor Knock Off ended a burned, -2, Choice-stripped Slaking.

protect_ledger_build16.payoff: Blocked Alakazam's Life Orb Psychic. Lethality is proven, not estimated: the identical attack KOed Weezing from full 149 HP on the very next turn. The guard bought the Gas one more turn, which is exactly the printed SUPPRESS tactic.

protect_summary_build16.note: One opponent Protect in eleven decision points. Weezing did not guard a second time; when it was about to die anyway on T2 it had no chance to choose, and Indeedee, Porygon2, Meloetta and Mega Staraptor - all four of which carry Protect - chose an action every single turn instead. No Wide Guard or Quick Guard exists on this team.

comparison_to_prior_receipt.prior_ledger_scope: receipt.json recorded six opponent Protects across three attempts (two losses and one win).
comparison_to_prior_receipt.decisive_attempt_detail: Prior attempt 3 (same party, same seed) had three opponent Protects - Weezing T1, Meloetta T6, Indeedee T8 - all with payoff, none empty, none consecutive. This rerun produced one, also with payoff. Norman was already clean on this axis before the fixes, so this room is a no-regression check rather than a repair measurement, and it passes: the fixes did not turn a guard-free body into a guarding one, and they did not remove the one guard that was correct.

prior_defects_retested.status: NOT REPRODUCED. Superficially it looks like it recurred - on turn 8 Meloetta chose Psychic at slot b0 and the log printed 'It doesn't affect Weavile...'. ai_defects_note: No AI defect observed in this run. Every opponent selection was defensible on the board as it stood at turn start: Slaking stayed Choice-correct, Porygon2 used Icy Wind as speed control while healthy and switched to Thunderbolt for the kill, Indeedee redirected rather than guarded, and Mega Staraptor picked the 4x Contrary attack. Two candidate 'defects' were inspected and rejected: Meloetta's Psychic whiff on turn 8 (caused by my own switch, see comparison_to_prior_receipt) and Indeedee dying to its own Follow Me on turn 4 (it pulled a Fighting-type attack off the ace, which is the point of the move).
level_rule_statement: NOT APPLIED, and here is why explicitly. The prior receipt's decision was KEEP. The rerun does not flip it. The brief's increase trigger is a first-attempt win with 0-1 player faints AND no real threat; the second half fails. Norman traded a critical High Horsepower KO on my Alakazam, took Gengar to 3 HP with a paralysis, took Spiritomb from 133 to 31, and the fight ran eleven decision points. The prior receipt also has two full optimized losses to this leader on the same lineage, which the brief's keep condition ('after a real fight') covers directly. The lower faint count versus the prior win is explained by a better player line - Parting Shot to -2 Attack plus a Will-O-Wisp on a loafing Slaking neutered the ace - not by the AI getting weaker. No opponent line in the teams file was touched.
could_this_be_cooler: Unchanged judgment from the prior receipt: keep the concept exactly. One genuine improvement did land since that receipt, and it matters for this question - with Follow Me now actually firing, the second half of the fight finally reads as the Psychic Terrain pair the dossier describes rather than as a Meloetta solo. That was the one thing the prior receipt named as making the leader read less well than it designs. No species, move, item, ability or EV change recommended.
